title: 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 Concludes At Bharat Mandapam New Delhi
subtitle:
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s Pavilion Records Total Sales of ₹2.38 Crore
Over 130 Artisans From 19 States Showcase India’s Traditional Craftsmanship, Indigenous Products And Cultural Heritage
body_text: The 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 concluded at Bharat Mandapam on Friday November 27, in the National Capital here, with Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s pavilion recording a total  sales of ₹ 2.38 crore, during the fair period from november 14 to 27, 2026. The strong response from visitors reflects growing appreciation for indigenous products, traditional craftsmanship and the entrepreneurial talent of artisans from across the country. The successful conclusion of the Ministry’s pavilion at the 45th IITF 2026 highlights the importance of providing artisans with platforms that connect their traditional skills and products with wider markets, thereby fostering economic empowerment and greater self-reliance. Located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, the Ministry’s pavilion served as a vibrant platform for showcasing India’s rich cultural heritage, traditional skills and indigenous craftsmanship. The participation of over 130 artisans from 19 States provided them with an opportunity to showcase their products, engage directly with customers and expand their market reach. A Senior Official in the Ministry Shri Sanjay Sharma said the artisans participated in the fair through the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC). Their participation reflects the Ministry’s continued efforts to promote entrepreneurship, strengthen market linkages and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs), he said. Shri Sharma said the pavilion featured an extensive range of traditional handlooms, intricately designed handicrafts, handcrafted jewellery, textiles, footwear, handmade articles and other indigenous products. Representing the distinctive artistic identities and cultural diversity of different regions, the products offered visitors an opportunity to experience and appreciate India's rich traditions of craftsmanship, he added. Shri Sharma informed that a key highlight of the Ministry’s participation was the promotion of TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme), aimed at establishing a distinct market identity for artisan-made products and enhancing their recognition among consumers. Through such initiatives, the Ministry seeks to bridge the gap between traditional craftsmanship and contemporary market requirements, encourage innovation and facilitate sustainable income-generating opportunities for artisans, he said. The Official remarked the encouraging sales performance during IITF 2026 underscores the importance of national-level exhibitions in enabling traditional artisans to enhance the visibility of their products, interact directly with customers, understand evolving consumer preferences, establish business networks and explore new market opportunities. He said participation in such platforms also contributes to strengthening entrepreneurial capabilities, expanding customer bases and building sustainable business prospects. Shri Sharma said the Ministry’s participation in IITF 2026 reaffirmed its commitment to promoting inclusive economic development, preserving traditional craftsmanship, strengthening grassroots entrepreneurship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 spearheaded by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s guiding principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas’.
